metaDescription: Office cleaning cost guides for US suites: $0.05–$0.20/sq ft, $35–$65/hr rates, and $90–$135 visit minimums. Run our calculator or compare quotes.
excerpt: Understand how US janitorial contractors calculate per-square-foot, hourly, and flat-rate office cleaning bids across suites from 500 to 50,000+ sq ft. Use these national pricing benchmarks, restroom line-item formulas, and contract audit steps to spot padded quotes before signing.
quickAnswer: Standard US commercial office cleaning costs $0.05 to $0.20 per square foot per visit, or $35 to $65 per labor hour for routine general cleaning and $55 to $95 per hour for specialty restoration or biohazard work. Most contractors enforce a $90 to $135 minimum per-visit fee plus $15 to $30 per restroom, so a 5,000 sq ft carpeted suite with two restrooms cleaned 3 times per week averages $458 to $773 per visit ($5,948 to $10,042 per month using 13.0 monthly visits).

blocks.text: Evaluating commercial janitorial bids without a transparent pricing model is where most office managers overpay—or accidentally hire an underinsured crew that cuts corners by week four. Across the United States, legitimate cleaning companies build every recurring proposal from the same four operational inputs: **cleanable square footage**, **restroom fixture counts**, **flooring material labor multipliers**, and **weekly service frequency**.

This national benchmark hub breaks down the exact formulas behind US commercial cleaning quotes. Whether you manage a [750 sq ft executive suite](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-750-sq-ft-office/) or oversee a multi-floor corporate campus, these unit rates let you reverse-engineer any vendor proposal down to implied labor hours and true per-visit margins.
National Office Cleaning Cost Benchmarks by Square Footage

Commercial cleaning rates per square foot follow a predictable economy of scale. Suites under 2,500 sq ft carry the highest unit rates—typically **$0.12 to $0.20 per sq ft per visit**—because technician drive time, security check-in, supply staging, and equipment setup stay fixed regardless of floor area. Once a building crosses 10,000 sq ft, base rates drop to **$0.07 to $0.12 per sq ft**, and facilities above 25,000 sq ft command **$0.05 to $0.10 per sq ft**.

Smaller suites also collide with trip-charge floors. Because a commercial vendor cannot dispatch an insured crew for less than **$90 to $135 per visit**, a [1,000 sq ft office](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-1000-sq-ft-office/) or [1,200 sq ft office](/office-cleaning-cost-guides/cost-to-clean-a-1200-sq-ft-office/) frequently pays an effective rate above $0.15 to $0.24 per sq ft once restrooms and minimums are factored in.

blocks.title: Restrooms and Minimums Drive Small-Suite Pricing
blocks.text: Base square-footage brackets do not absorb heavy plumbing sanitation. Standard US proposals add $15 to $30 per restroom per visit on top of floor area rates, and enforce a $90 to $135 minimum trip charge when total calculated square-footage labor falls below two billable hours.
Per-Square-Foot vs. Hourly vs. Flat-Rate Contract Pricing Models

US commercial cleaners use three billing structures, and knowing when each applies prevents budget surprises. Standard recurring maintenance usually converts calculated square-footage labor into a **fixed flat-rate monthly retainer**, whereas irregular scopes—such as medical decontamination, post-construction dust removal, or multi-coat VCT stripping—bill at **$55 to $95 per specialty hour** rather than the **$35 to $65 per hour** standard janitorial range.

Always check how a contractor translates weekly visits into a monthly invoice. Because a 365-day year averages **4.333 weeks per month** (52 weeks divided by 12 months), a 3x/week contract actually delivers **13.0 visits per month**, and a 5x/week weekday schedule delivers **21.65 visits per month**—not 12 or 20. Quotes built on a naive 4-week month either hide extra fifth-week invoices or inflate per-visit unit rates to absorb those extra days.

items: **Flat-Rate Monthly Retainer:** Best for recurring 2x to 7x/week office suites; locks in predictable billing across 4-week and 5-week calendar months using the 4.333 weeks/month multiplier.
**Per-Square-Foot Pricing ($0.05–$0.20/sq ft):** Most transparent for multi-suite comparisons and RFP scorecards, provided restroom counts, breakrooms, and floor care are itemized separately.

**Hourly Janitorial Billing ($35–$65/hr standard):** Common for day-porter coverage, initial deep cleans, or seasonal turnover where square footage fluctuates; avoid open-ended hourly billing for unattended night shifts without timeclock logs.
**Specialty & Restoration Hourly ($55–$95/hr):** Reserved for OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens cleanup, post-renovation HEPA vacuuming, high interior glass, and machine floor burnishing.

blocks.text: How Cleaning Frequency and Minimum Visit Fees Change Your Monthly Bill

Raising weekly cleaning frequency increases total monthly spend, yet it simultaneously lowers your **per-visit cost**. Infrequent schedules—such as monthly (1x/month at a **1.28x multiplier**) or biweekly (2.17 visits/month at **1.16x**)—accumulate heavy trash overflow, restroom mineral scale, and ground-in carpet soil that force technicians to scrub longer on arrival. Daily 5x/week (**0.90x**) and 7x/week (**0.87x**) accounts benefit from light, repeatable surface passes and tighter route density.

blocks.title: Watch for 4-Week Billing Traps in Retainer Proposals
blocks.text: If a bid quotes a suspiciously low monthly price for 3x/week service, check the fine print for a 12-visit monthly cap. A genuine year-round 3x/week contract averages 13.0 visits per month (52 weeks x 3 / 12). Vendors who quote 12 visits often omit service during the fifth week of the month or issue surprise supplemental invoices.
Flooring Surfaces, Restrooms, and Add-On Scope Multipliers

Two offices of identical square footage can vary by 17% or more in monthly janitorial cost based strictly on floor finish. **Polished concrete** carries a **0.95x multiplier** because an auto-scrubber or dust mop clears wide aisles rapidly, whereas **commercial carpet tiles** serve as the **1.00x baseline**. **VCT and LVT vinyl** add **1.04x** for neutral-pH damp mopping and periodic buffing, **mixed carpet and hard floors** add **1.05x** for dual tool setups, **engineered hardwood** adds **1.08x** for low-moisture microfiber care, and **ceramic tile and grout** reaches **1.12x** due to manual grout-line agitation.

Beyond flooring and **$15 to $30 per restroom**, four recurring add-ons explain most gaps between competing bids: **breakroom and kitchenette sanitation** ($12 to $25 per visit covering sinks, microwave interiors, fridge fronts, and cabinet pulls), **interior glass and conference partitions** ($15 to $35 per visit), **vendor-supplied paper and soap consumables** ($0.012 to $0.025 per sq ft per visit), and **amortized quarterly deep floor care** ($0.03 to $0.06 per sq ft per month for hot-water extraction or VCT scrub-and-recoat).

blocks.text: Crew Production Rates, Equipment Speed, and Labor-Hour Auditing

The fastest way to spot an unrealistic cleaning bid is to convert the monthly price back into implied technician hours. According to ISSA commercial cleaning production benchmarks, a trained office custodian averages roughly **3,500 sq ft per labor hour** across open workstations (typically **2,800 to 4,000 sq ft/hr** depending on cubicle density), plus **0.15 to 0.25 hours per restroom**. For a 5,000 sq ft office with two restrooms, credible vendors allocate **1.55 to 2.29 labor hours per visit**. Any bidder pricing that suite under $300/visit in a standard US metro is either paying below legal W-2 burden or skipping half the checklist.

Equipment selection directly determines whether crews actually achieve ISSA production speeds without kicking fine dust back onto desks. High-output vendors equip night crews with ergonomic [commercial backpack vacuums](/commercial-vacuums-and-floor-machines/best-commercial-backpack-vacuums-for-offices/) rather than slow, heavy uprights. For example, units like the **ProTeam Super Coach Pro 6** (6 qt capacity, 4-Level HEPA filtration, 11.5 lb chassis, 66 dBA sound rating), the **Hoover Commercial C2401 Shoulder Vac Pro** (6.4 qt capacity, HEPA media filtration, 9.2 lb weight, 66 dBA), and the **Atrix VACBP1 Ergo HEPA** (8 qt capacity, 99.97% HEPA filtration, 10.3 lb weight, 67 dBA) allow technicians to weave cleanly through tight workstation aisles and stairwells while maintaining indoor air quality.

blocks.title: OSHA, HazCom, and Certificate of Insurance (COI) Requirements
blocks.text: Every commercial janitorial contractor working in a US office must maintain Safety Data Sheets (SDS) under OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200), follow OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) protocols for restroom bio-hazards, and provide an active Certificate of Insurance naming your business as Additional Insured alongside statutory Workers' Compensation and a janitorial fidelity bond.
How to Audit Office Cleaning Proposals and Benchmark Your Rate
Before issuing an RFP or signing a 12-month renewal, run your floor plan through our interactive Office Cleaning Cost Calculator and audit competing bids side by side in the Quote Comparator.

items.name: Verify Cleanable vs. Rentable Square Footage
items.text: Subtract mechanical rooms, freight corridors, and landlord-maintained common lobbies from your lease's rentable square footage so you only pay for net cleanable suite area.

items.name: Lock In Restroom, Breakroom, and Glass Line Items
items.text: List exact restroom fixture counts, microwave/sink counts, and linear feet of interior conference glass in your scope of work so bidders cannot treat them as post-contract change orders.

items.name: Normalize Proposals to 4.333 Weeks per Month
items.text: Divide each monthly quote by exact annual visits divided by 12 (13.0 for 3x/week, 21.65 for 5x/week) to expose disguised per-visit rate inflation.

items.name: Audit W-2 Payroll Compliance and COI Endorsements
items.text: Reject any bid priced near $20 to $25 implied hourly rates; verify W-2 employee coverage, Workers' Compensation, and $1M/$2M General Liability to shield your company from joint-employer liability.

items.name: Separate Consumables From Janitorial Labor
items.text: Compare vendor-supplied tissue, roll towels, soap, and liners ($0.012–$0.025/sq ft/visit) against direct bulk ordering so supply markups stay transparent.

faqs.q: Why do commercial cleaning companies multiply weekly visits by 4.333 instead of 4?
faqs.a: A standard calendar year contains 52 weeks across 12 months, which equals 4.333 weeks per month (4.33 in rounded pricing engines). Using 4.333 ensures a 3x/week office receives 13.0 scheduled visits per month and a 5x/week office receives 21.65 visits per month on average, keeping your flat monthly retainer identical in four-week and five-week months without fifth-week surprise invoices.

faqs.q: What insurance and compliance documents should a US janitorial vendor provide before starting?
faqs.a: Require a current Certificate of Insurance (COI) showing at least $1,000,000 per occurrence and $2,000,000 aggregate Commercial General Liability naming your organization and property manager as Additional Insured, proof of statutory Workers' Compensation coverage for W-2 cleaners, and a janitorial dishonesty or fidelity bond covering key and access-card exposure.

faqs.q: Do Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice chemicals increase office cleaning contract costs?
faqs.a: Switching to Green Seal GS-37 or EPA Safer Choice concentrated neutral cleaners and dilution-control systems rarely adds more than 0% to 4% to a recurring contract, because modern dilution dispensers reduce chemical waste. The larger cost driver in LEED-certified green cleaning programs is usually upgrading to certified HEPA filtration vacuums and microfiber laundering protocols.

faqs.q: What tasks are usually excluded from standard office cleaning rates per square foot?
faqs.a: Routine per-square-foot contracts cover trash removal, dusting, vacuuming, damp mopping, and restroom/breakroom surface sanitation. They almost always exclude hot-water carpet extraction, VCT floor stripping and waxing, exterior window washing, high dusting above 8 to 10 feet, inside-fridge cleanouts, paper/soap consumables, and OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens biohazard remediation unless itemized as add-ons.

faqs.q: How do OSHA HazCom and Bloodborne Pathogens rules affect janitorial pricing?
faqs.a: Under OSHA Hazard Communication (29 CFR 1910.1200), contractors must maintain labeled secondary chemical bottles and accessible Safety Data Sheets (SDS) in your janitorial closet. When restroom or medical-suite scopes involve potential exposure to bodily fluids, OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens (29 CFR 1910.1030) requires hepatitis B vaccination access, PPE, and regulated spill kits, contributing to the $55 to $95 per hour specialty labor tier.
